name: Max Born
role: Co-author, with Heisenberg, of the report on quantum mechanics
bio: Born made Göttingen one of the three centres of the new physics. He recognised Heisenberg's 1925 scheme as matrix algebra and, with Jordan and Heisenberg, turned it into a theory. In the summer of 1926, applying Schrödinger's equation to collisions, he proposed that the wave determines only the probability of an outcome — the rule entered as a note added in proof. He is a friend and regular correspondent of Einstein, and the recipient of the dice letter.

contributions.title: Matrix mechanics
contributions.note: With Jordan, and with Heisenberg: the 'three-man paper'.

contributions.title: Statistical interpretation
contributions.note: Probability of an outcome proportional to |ψ|².

beliefs: The wave function determines probabilities; the probability evolves causally, the particle does not. He is inclined to give up determinism in atomic physics, while acknowledging that this is partly a philosophical choice.
philosophy: A mathematician's physicist, attentive to foundations. Less combative than Heisenberg or Pauli about interpretation; explicit that the renunciation of determinism is a decision informed by physics.

style.method: Mathematical clarification; appeal to collision experiments.
style.manner: Measured, candid about what is choice and what is proof.
avoid: Portraying him as a mere adjunct to Heisenberg

disagreements.topic: Whether the statistical interpretation is final

disagreements.note: Born's reading displaced Schrödinger's charge density.

horizonNotes.note: Decades later Pauli will tell him he has misunderstood Einstein's objection.
